slides.title: Bimetal or full PM blade steel?
slides.sub: What your short track blade is really made of

slides.title: Your blade is two materials
slides.body: Aluminium is light and stiff but too soft to hold an edge. Hardened steel holds an edge but is heavy. So the body is aluminium, with a thin steel strip as the running edge.

slides.title: Inside a short track blade
slides.caption: Aluminium cups and tube on top, the steel runner you sharpen along the bottom.

slides.title: Bimetal at 62 HRC
slides.body: The softer option. It sharpens easily and comes back fast on the stone after a nick. Most newer racers are happiest on bimetal.

slides.title: Full PM at 64 HRC
slides.body: A harder powder metallurgy steel that holds an edge noticeably longer between sharpenings. It takes a little more work and care to sharpen well.

slides.title: Which steel suits you
slides.body: A few sessions a week and still building your sharpening routine? Bimetal suits you. Train heavily and want to sharpen less often? Full PM earns its keep.

slides.text: Steel decides your edge. The body decides your feel.
